items.title: Gaslighting for God: The Secret Corporate Edits of the LDS Church
items.summary: A Mormon News Roundup YouTube video on how the LDS Church touts "continuous revelation" while making sudden edits to what it presents as eternal decrees.

items.title: BYUI student arrested on child exploitation charges
items.summary: The BYU-Idaho Scroll reports that Rexburg police arrested BYU-Idaho student Evan Cobb on Nov. 19 and charged him with two counts of distribution of sexually exploitative material; his bond was set at $100,000 and his next court hearing is Nov. 25.

items.title: LDS Bible Scholar Who Exposed Wesley Huff’s Plagiarism Demands Direct Apology Following Huff’s Confession
items.summary: ChurchLeaders reports that Latter-day Saint biblical scholar Dan McClellan, who raised plagiarism allegations against apologist Wesley Huff, says Huff still owes him and Huff’s dissertation supervisor direct apologies despite Huff’s public admission of plagiarism.

items.title: 11/20 – Why Does Ben McAdams Ignore Us?
items.summary: The Nov. 20 episode of the This Week in Latter-days podcast, titled "Why Does Ben McAdams Ignore Us?" (about 1 hour 22 minutes).

items.title: Missed the first three ticket releases? More Salt Lake Temple open house tickets coming soon
items.summary: The Deseret News reports the church will release a fourth batch of Salt Lake Temple open house tour tickets on Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 11 a.m. MST, after the first million tickets were claimed in less than 24 hours.

items.title: Mormon Bishop Resigns Amid Scandal, LDS Predator Watch & MAGA vs Mormon Media – Mormon News | Ep. 2233
items.summary: Mormon Stories' weekly Mormon News Podcast with John Dehlin and Meggan Hayes covers an Idaho Fish and Game commissioner and LDS bishop who resigned after agreeing to plead guilty to hunting violations, a Utah Primary teacher facing criminal charges, and criticism of LDS-owned media by Utah Republicans.

items.title: Utah’s housing crunch has churches asking, ‘What would Jesus do?’ to help
items.summary: KUER reports that a Lutheran congregation is planning affordable housing on its land, and that the Latter-day Saint church donated 2.5 acres and a historic recreation center for a 66-unit Salt Lake City development, with church general authority seventy John A. McCune saying more such projects are likely.

items.title: Wrestling with Richard
items.summary: In an Exponent II blog post, M. Alva Nilsson writes that the more fruitful discussion about Richard Wagner and Joseph Smith lies in what people do with what they created, whether or not they like them.
